content.text: {"answer":"Use mixed or variable precision at the expert level, and make the precision decision dynamically from routing and expert importance so critical experts stay higher-bit while less important ones are quantized more aggressively. For MoE on edge/mobile-class hardware, DyMoE is the most direct match: it dynamically quantizes experts at runtime with importance-aware prioritization, uses depth-adaptive scheduling to protect sensitive layers, and adds look-ahead prefetching to hide I/O stalls, yielding large TTFT and TPOT speedups on commercial edge hardware while preserving accuracy [2]. DPA-MoE is similar but controls precision after routing by allocating prefix-decodable weight chunks using live router gate scores, so one encoded checkpoint can run at multiple effective weight budgets with only modest throughput overhead [7].\n\nIf your target is specifically mobile NPUs, Quant.npu shows that mobile hardware may require fully static quantization, and it adds a sensitivity-guided adaptive mixed-precision scheme to trade off accuracy and latency, reducing latency on real mobile NPUs [4]. For bit allocation itself, GEMQ, AlphaQ, and NatScale differ in how they choose expert precisions: global optimization with router adaptation [5], calibration-free allocation from expert weight spectra [3], and contrast-calibrated objective-aware allocation [6].","grounded":true}
